messages.subject: Locale, again. Handling of special characters
parts:
I have read all the threads on locales here, but I believe it still has not been solved. See, for example


https://groups.google.com/d/topic/shiny-discuss/BO0nzLFirvQ/discussion

and my own:

https://groups.google.com/d/topic/shiny-discuss/4v5WcCdeGBg/discussion


Here is another approach, building on Stéphanes utility. Tested und Ubuntu LT and the current release version of the server.

# ui
library(shiny)
title <- "Mi sesión"
#title <- "My session"
Encoding(title) <- "UTF-8"

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel(title),
  sidebarPanel(),
  mainPanel(
    verbatimTextOutput("locale")
  )
))
  

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  output$locale <- renderPrint({ 
    sessionInfo()$locale 
  })
})

Scenarios: (sessionInfo below)
1) Use runApp()  with  title "Mi sesión"

Works ok, with something like 
[1] "LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8;LC_NUMERIC=C;LC_TIME=C;LC_COLLATE=C;LC_MONETARY=C;LC_MESSAGES=C;LC_PAPER=C;LC_NAME=C;LC_ADDRESS=C;LC_TELEPHONE=C;LC_MEASUREMENT=C;LC_IDENTIFICATION=C"

2) use shiny Server  "Mi sesión"


Note the Browser title

3) use shiny Server with My session

Note the C locale. This is what kills many of my string manipulations routines, and it is my main concern because I cannot use Umlauts. All is fine in runApp(), all Umlauthandling is strangely wrong (even with stringri function) and difficult to debug.

Dieter

messages.subject: Re: Locale, again. Handling of special characters
parts:
Partial solution, but not an explanation:

Setting 
Sys.setlocale('LC_CTYPE',"en_US.UTF-8")  

in ui.R works. I had tried it in server.r, and it fails there.

In a more complex case, where all my string handling in the package got garbled up, I had to move the Sys.setlocale close to the function that does Umlaut processing. So I assume at some place the RStudio server resets the locales to a not-so-good default.

I remember having read something similar in the shinyApps github forum by Yihui.

Dieter

I am running Ubuntu as a virtual Box installed with vagrant/puppet on Windows 7. Here is my setup

https://bitbucket.org/dmenne/rstudio-shiny-server-on-ubuntu

Here is my RStudio sessionInfo. As said: the application runs without the additional Sys.setlocale with shiny::runApp()

locale:
 [1] LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8 LC_NUMERIC=C         LC_TIME=C            LC_COLLATE=C       
 [5] LC_MONETARY=C        LC_MESSAGES=C        LC_PAPER=C           LC_NAME=C          
 [9] LC_ADDRESS=C         LC_TELEPHONE=C       LC_MEASUREMENT=C     LC_IDENTIFICATION=C

It looks like shiny server running on the same machine does not pick up these settings, and needs an explicit LC_Type. Without the explicit Sys.setlocale in global.R, all string processing plays very strange (most notoriously: factors!) when Umlauts are involved. I normally do not notice this because I avoid these if I can, but sometimes customers want their levels as "Prä" instead of "Pre".

Dieter

messages.author: 85e053d519f0f372
messages.subject: Re: Locale, again. Handling of special characters
parts:
One reason for the locale being C is that the environment variable
LANG is unset. You may check that using Sys.getenv('LANG') in R, or in
a terminal:

$ echo $LANG
en_US.utf8

If that is the case, one solution is to define LANG=C.UTF-8 or
en_US.UTF-8 in Renviron.site (depending what locales are available:
`locale -a`), so R can pick up a locale that is appropriate for
Unicode characters.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: 3ef7a01c7d912ca2
messages.subject: Re: Locale, again. Handling of special characters
parts:
My current solution is:

suppressWarnings(# gives warning on Windows
  Sys.setlocale('LC_CTYPE',"en_US.UTF-8")) # Very important for string and factor functions

However, I still consider it confusing that the program give different results when run on the same Unix with runApp or server. I believe this inconsistency should by handled by Shiny.

The most serious problem is not the bad string, but the fact that factors with Umlauts are dropped (i.e. NAed). I only noted this after I had the first "Prä" level, which was gone.

And the within-program inconsistent Umlaut-Handling in

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/shiny-discuss/4v5WcCdeGBg/N2dCdiZ_pC8J

should also be reviewed.



Dieter

messages.subject: Re: Locale, again. Handling of special characters
parts:
Again, the requirement to install Haskell/Pandoc from source was a wrong reading of the message that version 1.12 of Pandoc was required. It turned out that Pandoc was not found at all, but:

-- Under Windows/runApp everything ok
-- Under Ubuntu/runApp everything ok (!sic, I had not tested that before). So it means that Pandoc was found, and RStdudi also reports the correct RSTUDIO_PANDOC
-- Under Ubuntu-shinyServer, the 1.12 is required message comes up.

So again, it is the same story as with non-Ascii characters in the seperate thread you replied to: shiny-server does not pick up the environment.

The following helps, but it could lead to problems.

# global.R
if (!nzchar(Sys.getenv("RSTUDIO_PANDOC")))
  Sys.setenv(RSTUDIO_PANDOC = "/usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/pandoc")

Using a symlink works too, but I do not recommend this method. Your Pandoc is not standard and seems to work only with render/rmarkdown. Simply try -v or --version. So a global symlink could lead to problems in other parts of the system.

Dieter
